# VPN Troubleshooting Knowledge Base

## Overview
This article explains how to troubleshoot VPN connectivity issues for enterprise users.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that the VPN disconnects frequently, fails after a password reset, shows an authentication error, or cannot connect to the company network.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Confirm the user can log in to the Single Sign-On portal.
2. Ask the user to restart the VPN client.
3. Verify that Duo MFA approval is working.
4. Clear saved VPN credentials from the VPN client.
5. Confirm the user is using the latest VPN client version.
6. Ask the user to reconnect using the new password if the password was recently changed.

## Escalation
If the issue continues after these steps, route the ticket to Network Support.

## Ticket Category
VPN Connectivity

## Assigned Team
Network Support

## Default Priority
Medium

# Duo MFA Knowledge Base

## Overview
This article explains how to troubleshoot Duo Multi-Factor Authentication issues.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that they are not receiving Duo push notifications, cannot approve MFA, changed phones, or lost access to their authentication device.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Verify that the user has network connectivity on their mobile device.
2. Ask the user to open the Duo Mobile app manually.
3. Ask the user to check whether push notifications are enabled.
4. If the user changed phones, re-register the new device.
5. If the user lost the device, verify identity and issue a temporary bypass code according to policy.

## Escalation
If the user cannot complete MFA after basic troubleshooting, route the ticket to Identity and Access Management.

## Ticket Category
Multi-Factor Authentication

## Assigned Team
Identity and Access Management

## Default Priority
Medium

# Password Reset Knowledge Base

## Overview
This article explains how users can reset their enterprise account password and regain access to systems connected through Single Sign-On.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that they forgot their password, their account is locked, or they cannot log in after changing their password.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Ask the user to visit the enterprise Single Sign-On password reset portal.
2. Verify the user's identity using the approved recovery method.
3. Reset the password and wait 5 to 10 minutes for synchronization.
4. Ask the user to sign out of all active sessions.
5. Ask the user to log in again using the new password.
6. If the account is locked, wait for the lockout period or escalate to Identity and Access Management.

## Escalation
If the user cannot reset the password or the account remains locked, route the ticket to Identity and Access Management.

## Ticket Category
Account Access

## Assigned Team
Identity and Access Management

## Default Priority
Medium

# Ticket Priority Matrix

## Overview
This document defines priority levels for enterprise support tickets.

## Low Priority
Use Low priority when the issue has a workaround and does not block the user from working.

Examples:
- General software questions
- Minor UI issues
- Non-urgent access requests

## Medium Priority
Use Medium priority when one user is blocked from completing normal work but there is no company-wide impact.

Examples:
- One user cannot access VPN
- One user cannot log in to email
- One user needs password reset
- One user cannot approve Duo MFA

## High Priority
Use High priority when multiple users are affected or a business-critical team is blocked.

Examples:
- Multiple users cannot access VPN
- Department-wide email access issue
- Shared application outage

## Critical Priority
Use Critical priority when there is a production outage, security incident, or company-wide service disruption.

Examples:
- Production system outage
- Security breach
- Company-wide authentication failure

This article explains how users can reset their enterprise account password and regain access to systems connected through Single Sign-On.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that they forgot their password, their account is locked, or they cannot log in after changing their password.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Ask the user to visit the enterprise Single Sign-On password reset portal.
2. Verify the user's identity using the approved recovery method.
3. Reset the password and wait 5 to 10 minutes for synchronization.
4. Ask the user to sign out of all active sessions.
5. Ask the user to log in again using the new password.
6. If the account is locked, wait for the lockout period or escalate to Identity and Access Management.

## Escalation
If the user cannot reset the password or the account remains locked, route the ticket to Identity and Access Management.

## Ticket Category
Account Access

## Assigned Team
Identity and Access Management

## Default Priority
Medium

# Ticket Priority Matrix

## Overview
This document defines priority levels for enterprise support tickets.

## Low Priority
Use Low priority when the issue has a workaround and does not block the user from working.

Examples:
- General software questions
- Minor UI issues
- Non-urgent access requests

## Medium Priority
Use Medium priority when one user is blocked from completing normal work but there is no company-wide impact.

Examples:
- One user cannot access VPN
- One user cannot log in to email
- One user needs password reset
- One user cannot approve Duo MFA

## High Priority
Use High priority when multiple users are affected or a business-critical team is blocked.

Examples:
- Multiple users cannot access VPN
- Department-wide email access issue
- Shared application outage

## Critical Priority
Use Critical priority when there is a production outage, security incident, or company-wide service disruption.

Examples:
- Production system outage
- Security breach
- Company-wide authentication failure

# VPN Troubleshooting Knowledge Base

## Overview
This article explains how to troubleshoot VPN connectivity issues for enterprise users.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that the VPN disconnects frequently, fails after a password reset, shows an authentication error, or cannot connect to the company network.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Confirm the user can log in to the Single Sign-On portal.
2. Ask the user to restart the VPN client.
3. Verify that Duo MFA approval is working.
4. Clear saved VPN credentials from the VPN client.
5. Confirm the user is using the latest VPN client version.
6. Ask the user to reconnect using the new password if the password was recently changed.

## Escalation
If the issue continues after these steps, route the ticket to Network Support.

## Ticket Category
VPN Connectivity

## Assigned Team
Network Support

## Default Priority
Medium

# Duo MFA Knowledge Base

## Overview
This article explains how to troubleshoot Duo Multi-Factor Authentication issues.

## Common Symptoms
Users may report that they are not receiving Duo push notifications, cannot approve MFA, changed phones, or lost access to their authentication device.

## Troubleshooting Steps
1. Verify that the user has network connectivity on their mobile device.
2. Ask the user to open the Duo Mobile app manually.
3. Ask the user to check whether push notifications are enabled.
4. If the user changed phones, re-register the new device.
5. If the user lost the device, verify identity and issue a temporary bypass code according to policy.

## Escalation
If the user cannot complete MFA after basic troubleshooting, route the ticket to Identity and Access Management.

## Ticket Category
Multi-Factor Authentication

## Assigned Team
Identity and Access Management

## Default Priority
Medium
